items.context: Do you want to escalate your complaint?
Can you provide your complaint ID?

items.text: I have called multiple times but no solution has been given
The issue with my internet has not been fixed since last week
I want to speak to your senior officer right now please
My complaint was registered two weeks ago but there is no update
Every time I call they just say they will fix it but nothing happens
Please transfer my complaint to your supervisor immediately

items.context: Can you tell me what the complaint is about?
items.text: It is about my broadband connection not working properly

items.context: Can you share your previous complaint reference number?
items.text: My last complaint reference number is 987654321

items.context: Can you explain why you want to escalate the complaint?
items.text: I am frustrated because the service technician never came at scheduled time

items.context: Have you tried troubleshooting the issue yourself before calling us?
items.text: Yes I have already tried resetting the modem many times but no success
I have been facing frequent network disconnections for over a month now and every time I report the issue no permanent solution is provided so I want this escalated to your higher management
My previous complaint regarding call drop issue was registered on 5th March but till today no action has been taken and I am not satisfied with the response given by your customer care team

items.context: Why do you want your complaint to be escalated?
items.text: I want to escalate because this is the third time I am calling about the slow internet speed and the problem still persists

items.context: Can you please explain why this complaint is urgent for you?
items.text: I need the matter to be looked into seriously as my work depends on a stable network connection and this is causing me a lot of trouble

request.system:
You write realistic things that customers say to a voice agent on a phone call in India.
Write what the customer says out loud, as speech recognition would transcribe it:
natural spoken word order, fillers kept, no punctuation needed.
Each utterance is one complete customer turn: the customer has finished speaking
and is waiting for the agent to reply.
request.user:
Domain: telecom
Intent: escalate_complaint - is unhappy that an earlier complaint was not solved and wants escalation
Language: Indian English, Latin script.
Style for this batch: plain and direct

Write exactly 18 different customer turns in these six groups:
- "short": exactly 2 turns of 1-4 words (for example 'yes please', 'tomorrow', 'card ending 4321'),
- "short_with_context": exactly 2 turns of 1-4 words, each with the agent's question before it,
- "medium": exactly 6 turns of 5-12 words,
- "medium_with_context": exactly 4 turns of 5-12 words, each with the agent's question before it,
- "long": exactly 2 turns of 13-30 words,
- "long_with_context": exactly 2 turns of 13-30 words, each with the agent's question before it.
In the *_with_context groups, "context" is the question the agent asked just before that turn.
Vary people, amounts, dates, names and places. Do not number them. Do not start two turns the same way.
Return JSON: {"short": [{"text": "..."}, ...], "short_with_context": [{"text": "...", "context": "..."}, ...],
"medium": [...], "medium_with_context": [...], "long": [...], "long_with_context": [...]}
Every turn and question must be in Latin script.
